name: openWakeWord hey jarvis (tflite)
summary: Wake-word model that scores 80 ms frames of 16 kHz mono audio for the spoken phrase "hey jarvis", run through openWakeWord's TensorFlow Lite pipeline. Same model as openwakeword.hey-jarvis, packaged for consumers that run tflite_runtime instead of onnxruntime.

license.notes: Non-commercial only: the upstream repository's LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 but that covers the code, and openWakeWord's README licenses all included pre-trained models, this one among them, under CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.

notes: All three tflite artifacts are required together: melspectrogram.tflite and embedding_model.tflite are openWakeWord's shared preprocessor and must be passed as melspec_model_path / embedding_model_path with inference_framework="tflite"; openWakeWord otherwise resolves them inside its own package directory (openwakeword/resources/models/) and fails rather than fetching anything - the download only happens on an explicit openwakeword.utils.download_models() call. Vetted 2026-07-30 on Linux x86_64 with openwakeword 0.6.0 + tflite_runtime 2.14.0: instantiated with inference_framework="tflite" and predict() run over silence and noise frames (TFLite XNNPACK delegate active). IMPORTANT: tflite_runtime 2.14.0 is built against NumPy 1.x - it aborts with 'AttributeError: _ARRAY_API not found' under NumPy 2.x, so pin numpy<2 (verified here on numpy 1.26.4). The ONNX packaging (openwakeword.hey-jarvis) has no such constraint.
